newsitem.title: UK: Anglo-French rail jv seals Thameslink subsidy-free.
newsitem.headline: Anglo-French rail jv seals Thameslink subsidy-free.

text.p: British public transport operator Go-Ahead Group Plc and its French joint venture partner Generale du Transport Industriel(VIA G.T.I.) have agreed to run the Thameslink train operating company and will pay Britain an average premium over the seven-year life of the contract, the government announced on Tuesday.
"This represents an average premium of 17 million stg per annum in current prices over the life of the franchise," the Office of Passenger Rail Franchising(Opraf) said in a statement.

The Thameslink passenger rail franchise operates services between Bedford and Luton to the north of London and Brighton on the south coast, connecting Gatwick Airport with northern and central London.

GOVIA has committed to operate at least the current number of train miles for the length of the franchise and to a number of service enhancements, including more early morning and off-peak trains to serve the Gatwick line, Opraf said.
In addition, the venture has committed to investments in improved stations, enhanced passenger security and rolling stock refurbishment.
Unlike many of the other 20 or so franchises for which final terms have already been agreed, GOVIA will receive a subsidy at the start of the contract term only and this will soon reverse.
From receiving 2.5 million stg in subsidy in year one, it will move to paying Opraf a premium of 28.4 million stg in 2004.

During the latter part of this franchise preparations should be underway for the planned Thameslink 2000 project, which is intended to further expand the destination range covered by the service and provide new rail links across south east England.
The line's passenger revenue for the year to March 31, 1996 was 76 million stg and as at July 20 it employed 522 staff.
